findings.evidence: `grep -o ivt mathlib/Mathlib` → 4 hits, all a local name in `RingTheory/Morita/Matrix.lean`; Mathlib spells the notion `intermediate_value_Icc` (`Topology/Order/IntermediateValue.lean:586`) and root existentials `exists_root_of_degree_eq_one` (`Algebra/Polynomial/FieldDivision.lean:536`). The same file uses `intermediate_value_Icc` at line 148, so `ivt` is inconsistent even locally.
findings.fix: Rename to conclusion-describing names, e.g. `Polynomial.exists_isRoot_Ioo_of_eval_neg_of_eval_pos` and `Polynomial.exists_isRoot_Ioo_of_eval_mul_neg`.
findings.issue: `ivt` (and `ivt_of_mul_neg`, line 140) is an acronym that is not Mathlib terminology and does not describe the conclusion (`∃ c ∈ Ioo a b, p.eval c = 0`).

findings.evidence: `Grep "SquareClosed" code/TauCeti --glob *.lean` returns only these three declarations and their call sites; `Grep "SquareClosed|IsSqClosed|sqClosed" mathlib/Mathlib` → no matches.
findings.fix: Drop the phantom namespace and name the hypothesis: `finrank_eq_one_of_forall_isSquare`, `isAlgClosed_of_forall_isSquare`, `finrank_eq_one_of_isGalois_of_forall_isSquare`. Same for the `_of_isSquare`/`hsq` names `finrank_ne_two_of_isSquare` (FiniteExtension.lean:32) and `finrank_eq_one_of_twoGroup` (Galois.lean:41), whose hypothesis is also a `∀`.
findings.issue: `SquareClosed.finrank_eq_one`, `SquareClosed.isAlgClosed` (line 55) and `SquareClosed.finrank_eq_one_of_isGalois` (Galois.lean:55) sit in a `SquareClosed` namespace for which no declaration exists, so dot notation can never fire (the hypothesis is `hsq : ∀ x : C, IsSquare x`).

findings.evidence: Mathlib keeps the two families distinct: `monotoneOn_of_deriv_nonneg` (`Analysis/Calculus/Deriv/MeanValue.lean:411`) vs `monotone_of_deriv_nonneg` (:419); `strictMonoOn_of_deriv_pos` (:376) vs `strictMono_of_deriv_pos` (:388); `antitoneOn_of_deriv_nonpos` (:480); `strictAntiOn_of_deriv_neg` (:444).
findings.issue: `Rolle.monotone` proves `MonotoneOn p.eval (Icc a b)`, not `Monotone`; likewise `Rolle.antitone` (60), `Rolle.strictMono` (70), `Rolle.strictAnti` (78). The names advertise the global predicates.

findings.evidence: The lemmas they call are `irreducible_quadratic_eval_pos_iff_leadingCoeff_pos` / `..._eval_neg_iff_leadingCoeff_neg` (`code/TauCeti/Algebra/Polynomial/RealClosed/Quadratic.lean:82,93`). Counterexample to the unqualified name: `p = X^2 - 1` over ℝ has `natDegree = 2`, `eval 0 * eval 2 = -1 * 3 < 0`.
findings.fix: Rename to `irreducible_quadratic_eval_mul_pos` and `irreducible_quadratic_leadingCoeff_mul_eval_pos`, matching the sibling lemmas.
findings.issue: `quadratic_eval_mul_pos` omits the essential `Irreducible p` hypothesis from the name, so the name asserts something false for quadratics in general; `quadratic_leading_mul_pos` (line 47) has the same defect and additionally abbreviates `leadingCoeff` to `leading` and drops `eval`.

findings.evidence: Naming conventions, "Predicates as suffixes": `IsClosed (Icc a b)` → `isClosed_Icc`; Mathlib's own real-closed file uses prefix form (`IsRealClosed.isSquare_neg_of_not_isSquare`, `nonneg_iff_isSquare`, `mathlib/Mathlib/FieldTheory/IsRealClosed/Basic.lean:76,111`), and all `QuadraticAlgebra` lemmas live in that namespace (`mathlib/Mathlib/Algebra/QuadraticAlgebra/Basic.lean:44`).
findings.issue: `complex_isSquare` puts the predicate last and calls `QuadraticAlgebra R (-1) 0` "complex", which is not Mathlib terminology; its first explicit argument is `z : QuadraticAlgebra R (-1) 0`, so it belongs in the `QuadraticAlgebra` namespace. `complex_isAlgClosed` (AlgebraicClosed.lean:68) has the same predicate-suffix and terminology problem.

findings.evidence: Mathlib has no `TwoGroup`; the notion is `IsPGroup p G` (`mathlib/Mathlib/GroupTheory/PGroup.lean:64,86`), and the statements here are literally `IsPGroup 2 (E ≃ₐ[R] E)`.
findings.issue: `galois_isTwoGroup` and `finrank_eq_one_of_twoGroup` (line 41) use nonstandard "twoGroup" for `IsPGroup 2`, and the first puts the predicate in suffix position.

findings.fix: Name them after the conclusion, e.g. `exists_derivative_eval_eq_zero_of_eval_eq_zero_of_forall_ne_zero` and `exists_derivative_eval_eq_zero_of_eval_eq_zero`.
findings.issue: `rolle_consecutive` and `rolle_roots` (line 93) conclude `∃ c ∈ Ioo a b, p.derivative.eval c = 0`, not `Rolle _`; since this PR defines a Prop `Rolle` (Rolle.lean:27) whose proofs are named `rolle_*` (`rolle_realClosed : Rolle R`, line 113), the `rolle_` prefix misreads as "concludes `Rolle`".

findings.evidence: Mathlib's mean value theorem is `exists_deriv_eq_slope` / `exists_ratio_deriv_eq_ratio_slope` (`mathlib/Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/Deriv/MeanValue.lean:153,133`); no Mathlib declaration is named `mean_value`.
findings.issue: `Rolle.mean_value` names the classical theorem rather than its conclusion `p.eval b - p.eval a = p.derivative.eval c * (b - a)`.

findings.evidence: Rubric's dot-notation rule; repo precedent: `Grep "namespace Polynomial" code/TauCeti` and `Grep "_root_\.Polynomial\." code/TauCeti` give dozens of hits (e.g. `TauCeti/Algebra/Polynomial/LinearFactor.lean:42`, `TauCeti/RingTheory/Polynomial/Roots.lean:58`).
findings.fix: Put these `eval`/root lemmas in the `Polynomial` namespace (`_root_.Polynomial.…`), as the rest of the repo does for polynomial lemmas.
findings.issue: `eval_mul_pos_of_no_roots`, `ivt` (125), `ivt_of_mul_neg` (140) and `rolle_consecutive`/`rolle_roots` (AbstractRolle.lean:45,93) all take an explicit `p : R[X]` first but live in `TauCeti.RealClosure`, so `p.eval_mul_pos_of_no_roots` does not elaborate and upstreaming needs a rename — while the same file puts `intermediate_value_Icc` in `Polynomial` (line 148).

summary: Several introduced names describe the classical theorem rather than the conclusion (`ivt`, `rolle_consecutive`, `mean_value`), use nonstandard terminology (`twoGroup`, `complex_`, `leading`), overstate the statement (`Rolle.monotone` proves only `MonotoneOn`; `quadratic_eval_mul_pos` needs irreducibility), and hang three theorems off a `SquareClosed` namespace that does not exist. No notation is introduced.
